reason: Classification of Jacobian elliptic fibrations on Km(E1xE2) is published (Oguiso 1989: 11 fibrations for non-isogenous; Kuwata-Shioda 2006 give Weierstrass models/parameters; Kumar and others for Km(ExE)), so the enumeration half is textbook. No published or filed use of these fibrations for Semaev/IC decomposition: web searches (Kummer/elliptic fibration + Semaev/ECDLP) returned only generic Semaev/Weil-descent literature; atlas/corpus grep found no card on elliptic fibrations of the S_3 surface. Closure collisions: (1) LEAD-EXO-curve-model-representation (closed_obstructed) says Kummer line is Bezout-optimal among E->P^1 coordinates; its scope_limits explicitly say 'Kummer surfaces of products' are NOT addressed, and revisit_when = 'a coordinate E->P^1 with degree below Kummer degree' - the idea is not a coordinate on E so not directly covered. (2) Symmetric e1,e2 lattice for S_3 closed (MAP_closed Coppersmith entry) - bidegree<=(1,1) parameters such as x1+x2, x1x2, x1/x2 are exactly those symmetric/product coordinates, and projections x1,x2 have bidegree (1,0), so the stated prediction 'some fibration has bidegree<=(1,1)' is trivially true and uninformative. (3) Fibre-wise, a base parameter t(x1,x2) is a change of variables on the same ideal; solving degree is invariant except via presentation-dependent d_F (closed: first fall degree is a constant of the presentation; last fall degree presentation dependent, growth open lever 1). Weil descent needs x1,x2 in an F_2-subspace, which a rational t does not preserve, so descent 'at lower degree' needs t-fibre conditions not subspace conditions - no mechanism given. Same-ideal Bezout/degree conservation makes 'relabelling' the expected outcome. Transport-conservation lemma does not cover this (non-homomorphic) but GHS/cover scope note does.
